notes: A representative slice of crates/web-host/src/shim/kernel32.rs, where about fifty bindings live. Handles are plain addresses here: the guest never dereferences a heap handle it received.

functions.name: GetVersion
functions.description: Claim Windows XP 5.1 (build 2600) so the version checks take the branch the art was drawn for. The localization's own volume fix targets newer versions separately.
functions.evidence: trace: called once during CRT init, result compared against 0x80000000 in the guest's startup path

functions.name: GetModuleHandleA
functions.description: The image base. The guest passes null and expects its own module; there is exactly one module in this host.
functions.evidence: trace: null argument at instruction 184412, result reused as the instance handle in RegisterClassA

functions.name: GetLastError
functions.description: Reports the error the previous shim chose to set, so a caller that checks after a refusal sees the code Windows would have produced.
functions.evidence: trace: read immediately after LoadLibraryA in the CRT's DLL probe

functions.name: HeapAlloc
functions.description: The game allocates and frees every frame; the arena is bump-with-reuse so the churn does not consume the reserve. A request the arena cannot hold answers NULL, which is what the guest's own out-of-memory path tests for.
functions.evidence: trace: 4-10 calls per frame during the board; size histogram peaks at 160 bytes

functions.name: HeapFree
functions.description: Returns the block to the free list. Without this the per-frame churn grows the arena until the host reports heap_used climbing without bound.
functions.evidence: trace: paired one-for-one with HeapAlloc in the same routine

functions.name: Sleep
functions.description: Must not block: a blocking sleep would freeze the page, and the frame clock already owns pacing.
functions.evidence: trace: called on the game's own frame limit; frame time is unchanged with the stub

functions.name: IsBadReadPtr
functions.description: Answers "the pointer is fine" so the CRT's own validation never short-circuits a real access. The memory layer checks every access anyway and reports the fault with an address.
functions.evidence: trace: the CRT probes its own stack buffers, which are always valid

functions.name: LoadLibraryA
functions.description: There are no further libraries to load: every needed DLL is a shim table in this host. Answering null with the matching error lets the CRT take its missing-DLL path instead of hanging.
functions.evidence: trace: probes DSETUP.dll and then continues with its own defaults

functions.name: GlobalLock
functions.description: Every handle the game holds is already a stable pointer, so locking is identity. Returning null here would make the guest treat a valid block as unavailable.
functions.evidence: trace: called on handles produced by GlobalAlloc, which this host does not move

functions.name: lstrcmpiA
functions.description: Known-incomplete: this says every pair of strings is equal. It is safe for the one call site that compares a name it just wrote, and it is recorded here as a stub rather than a result to trust.
functions.evidence: trace: one call site, used as a cache-key probe whose miss is harmless
